overview: This table controls how each attack follows, turns toward, or teleports to its target.
description: Per-attack homing behavior: movement/rotation curves, range and timing gates, warp placement, ground following, armor and external push effects.

Id.simple: The name that connects this tracking setup to a specific attack or follow-up attack.
Id.technical: FName Unreal DataTable row key (exported as ID). Attack actions resolve ActionHomingDataTables by AttackRow.Id_ActionHoming or Id_CancelAttackActionHoming through Action_FindActionHomingRow (bCheckNone=true, so None resolves to no row); FName comparison is case-insensitive. Character-specific actions and shikigami also look up hardcoded ids, and ResolveActionHomingId overrides can remap or suppress the id before lookup (CP_110, CP_130, CP_210, CN_240). The manager loads all five numbered shards into one ordered array and the first table containing the id supplies the row. Exported rows use ids such as CP_010_ATTACKA_01.

ActionHomingType.simple: Chooses how the attack follows its target, including stick direction, curving, teleporting, or moving in before a teleport.
ActionHomingType.technical: uint8-backed EGameActionHomingType switch in StartHoming/TickHoming. None/Curve use target steering or the default branch; EightWay derives direction from stick angle bands; Warp teleports to the computed warp location; WarpMove moves toward it before teleporting. StartHoming returns immediately when Homing_Time_Max <= 0. Only Warp (not WarpMove) uses AttackRow animations in StartAttackHoming. The shikigami StartHoming stores the type but its tick uses the basic steering path. Invalid=255 exists in the enum; no exported row uses EightWay or Invalid.

CharacterAnimation.simple: Which character animation plays when tracking starts, for moving teleports and ordinary attacks. Plain teleports use the attack's own animation.
CharacterAnimation.technical: FName. Character attacks play it in StartAttackHoming when the armed row's type is neither Warp nor WarpMove; Warp and WarpMove instead take CharacterAnimation from AttackRow. Shikigami attacks unconditionally play this homing-row FName when their homing is active. If homing timed out (HomingResult == 0) and CharacterAnimation_Failure is None, ActivateAttack continues to PlayAnimationDefault(AttackRow.CharacterAnimation); on non-timeout activation it returns without playing an animation if that AttackRow name is None or the homing type is Warp. Exported names are animation keys, not montage asset paths.

CharacterAnimation_Failure.simple: Which animation plays when the attack loses its target before connecting. Leaving this empty keeps the normal attack animation.
CharacterAnimation_Failure.technical: FName. If HomingResult == 0 and this name is non-None, ActivateAttack plays it and clears super/hyper armor and bByte1E9 before returning. None means normal attack activation proceeds.

WeaponAnimation.simple: Which weapon animation plays when tracking starts for ordinary attacks and moving teleports. Plain teleports use the attack's own weapon animation.
WeaponAnimation.technical: FName passed to PlayWeaponAnimation when character homing arms for any type other than Warp/WarpMove; those two take WeaponAnimation from AttackRow. None skips playback in StartAttackHoming. ActivateAttack's later weapon playback also uses AttackRow.WeaponAnimation only on its normal fall-through path.

Inertia_Rate.simple: How strongly the character keeps sliding after this attack stops tracking. Higher values give a stronger slide.
Inertia_Rate.technical: Float magnitude passed to SetInertia with EaseOut when arrival, timeout, warp exit or WarpMove completion ends homing; bFollowGroundEnabled is the follow-ground flag in most character paths (Warp uses false; shikigami and CN_081's hit-quota early exit use false). CN_081 also applies it directly from the cached row on a hit quota.

Inertia_Time.simple: How long the character keeps sliding after the attack stops tracking. Longer settings make the slide last longer.
Inertia_Time.technical: Seconds passed with Inertia_Rate to SetInertia on homing termination paths.

Rotation_Yaw.simple: Turns the character's starting aim a little to the side when tracking begins. Most attacks keep the aim straight at the target.
Rotation_Yaw.technical: Degrees. 0 means rotate directly toward the target (subject to Rotation_Angle_Limit); non-zero rotates the flattened target heading by this angle about Z, then uses StartRotationEase over Rotation_Time.

Rotation_Time.simple: How long the character takes to turn toward the target, with shorter times feeling quicker. A negative setting turns this turn off.
Rotation_Time.technical: Seconds. RotateTowardTarget / RotateTowardLocation / StartRotationEase start an EEasingFunc::Linear ease with blend exponent 2.0 only when Time >= 0; the exported -1.0 value (9 rows) is therefore a sentinel that suppresses the rotation ease. EightWay also uses it to rotate to the stick-derived destination.

Rotation_Angle_Limit.simple: How far off-center the target may be before the character turns to face it. Keeping this low allows turns at any angle.
Rotation_Angle_Limit.technical: Degrees. In the default branch with Rotation_Yaw == 0, RotateTowardTarget is called only when this limit is <= 0 or >= the angle between owner forward and target. 0 effectively disables the angle gate.

Rotation_Speed_Start.simple: How fast the character first turns while following the target. Higher values start the turn faster.
Rotation_Speed_Start.technical: Degrees/second-style value passed to State4B8.RotationSpeedInterp.Start with Rotation_Speed_End and Rotation_Speed_InterpolateTime. The interpolator is armed only when a secondary target exists.

Rotation_Speed_End.simple: How fast the character is turning by the end of the turn. Higher values finish the turn faster.
Rotation_Speed_End.technical: Second value of RotationSpeedInterp.Start; see Rotation_Speed_Start.

Rotation_Speed_InterpolateTime.simple: How long the turn speed takes to change from its starting value to its ending value.

Rotation_Speed_EasingType.simple: Chooses how the turn speed changes, with the usual setting easing out gently near the end.
Rotation_Speed_EasingType.technical: EGameEasingType converted by ShikigamiMovement_ToEasingFunc before RotationSpeedInterp.Start.

Rotation_Speed_Blend_Exp.simple: Shapes how the turn speed changes during the move. The exact feel of this setting is unclear.
Rotation_Speed_Blend_Exp.technical: Float passed as the blend exponent in RotationSpeedInterp.Start.

Speed_Start.simple: How fast the character begins moving while following the target, scaled by Cursed Energy attack rate for fighters and used directly by shikigami.
Speed_Start.technical: Units/second. Character homing starts State4B8.SpeedInterp at GetCP240PassiveRate() * Speed_Start (the passive rate is read for both endpoints); TickHoming updates it each step after Homing_Delay_Time. The shikigami path uses Speed_Start and Speed_End directly without that multiplier.

Speed_End.simple: How fast the character moves by the end of the approach, scaled by Cursed Energy attack rate for fighters and used directly by shikigami.
Speed_End.technical: Units/second, also multiplied by GetCP240PassiveRate() before interpolation for characters (raw for shikigami). CP_010 exports 1500.

Speed_InterpolateTime.simple: How long the character takes to go from the starting speed to the ending speed while tracking.

Speed_EasingType.simple: Chooses how the movement speed changes during the approach, with the usual setting slowing gently near the end.
Speed_EasingType.technical: EGameEasingType converted by ShikigamiMovement_ToEasingFunc in SpeedInterp.Start.

Speed_Blend_Exp.simple: Shapes how the movement speed changes during the approach. The exact feel of this setting is unclear.
Speed_Blend_Exp.technical: Float passed as the blend exponent in SpeedInterp.Start.

HomingDistance.simple: How far away the target can be before the attack uses its shorter tracking time. Some characters also use this distance to repeat attacks.
HomingDistance.technical: World units. At StartHoming, if a secondary target is farther than this positive distance, HomingTime is set to Homing_Time_Min instead of Homing_Time_Max. CP_051 also gates attack repeats by Distance <= HomingDistance; CP_051's warp-start gates use WarpDistance instead.

Homing_Delay_Time.simple: How long the character waits before moving toward the target after tracking begins. This also delays a teleport.
Homing_Delay_Time.technical: Seconds. TickHoming accumulates HomingElapsed and returns without moving while elapsed < Homing_Delay_Time. This check runs for every armed type after the non-warp arrival and timeout checks; it is not skipped by Warp/WarpMove, so it also delays a warp teleport or WarpMove completion. The shikigami tick applies the same delay.

Homing_Time_Min.simple: The shorter tracking time used when the target is far away. Moving teleports also finish within this time if they have not arrived.
Homing_Time_Min.technical: Seconds. Selected at StartHoming when the target is beyond HomingDistance; WarpMove also completes when Homing_Time_Min <= elapsed even if the warp destination has not been reached. It is 0.0 in 149 exported rows, which makes the post-delay timeout immediate when that branch is selected.

Homing_Time_Max.simple: How long the attack can keep following its target. A value of zero turns tracking off.
Homing_Time_Max.technical: Seconds. StartHoming returns immediately when this is <= 0; otherwise it initializes HomingTime, and non-warp homing exits by timeout when HomingTime <= HomingElapsed.

bIgnoreHomingRange.simple: Chooses whether the attack stops when it gets close enough to the target. Turning this on skips that closeness check.
bIgnoreHomingRange.technical: Bool. When false, TickHoming calls IsOutsideHomingRange with Distance_Correct and Z ranges to decide arrival; when true this check is skipped and only follow-ground blocking, delay/time or warp logic can end homing.

Distance_Correct.simple: Adds extra room to the closeness check, changing how near the character must be to count as arriving.
Distance_Correct.technical: World units passed with owner/target capsule radii to IsOutsideHomingRange in normal and WarpMove arrival checks.

RangeZ_Upper.simple: How high above the target the character may be and still count as close enough. This applies when ground following is off.
RangeZ_Upper.technical: World units. Copied into RangeUpper only when homing ignores ground following; if both characters hit ground and the ceiling trace finds no hit, upper/lower are cleared. Used in IsOutsideHomingRange and WarpMove passage tests.

RangeZ_Lower.simple: How far below the target the character may be and still count as close enough. This applies when ground following is off.
RangeZ_Lower.technical: World units, paired with RangeZ_Upper in the same arrival/range tests.

AngleZ.simple: How steeply the character may travel upward or downward while following the target. Larger angles allow steeper paths when ground following is off.
AngleZ.technical: Degrees. TickHomingMove reads the row value when ground-following is disabled; if the angle between direction and the flattened horizontal vector exceeds it, direction is rotated about the right axis by -AngleZ (sign flips when the owner is above the target) and target steering is disabled.

WarpDistance.simple: How far ahead the game searches for a teleport landing spot. For closer targets it searches around the target.
WarpDistance.technical: World units. GameWarp_ComputeWarpLocation takes the far-target branch when WarpDistance > 0 and is less than the 3D distance to the target (or the target is invalid), sweeping a capsule from the owner toward the target to WarpDistance minus owner radius; the pitch/yaw-adjusted WarpDirection is used for the near-target heading/candidate ring, not that initial sweep. CP_051 gates warp-start effects by Distance <= WarpDistance.

WarpTargetDistance.simple: How much space the game leaves around the target when choosing a teleport landing spot. One character uses this to cancel tracking up close.
WarpTargetDistance.technical: World units added to the target capsule radius to form ReachDistance for the near-target candidate ring (2 steps x 4 turns). BlowSimulate can replace ReachDistance with a prediction-based value on walls. CN_240 also reads it to suppress CN_240_ATTACKB_01 homing when the target is already within that range.

WarpDirectionAdjustPitch.simple: Tilts the teleport approach upward or downward when choosing a landing spot near the target. Faraway teleports keep the straight approach.
WarpDirectionAdjustPitch.technical: Degrees. The flat direction toward the target is rotated about the direction quaternion's Y axis by this pitch to form WarpDirection for the near-target heading/candidate ring; the far-target sweep uses the raw owner-to-target vector. Exported values are 0 except a few 15/30/60/80/90 rows.

WarpDirectionAdjustYaw.simple: Turns the teleport approach sideways near the target. A half-turn also changes the camera after a moving teleport.
WarpDirectionAdjustYaw.technical: Degrees. Rotates WarpDirection about Z for near-target placement; the far-target sweep is unadjusted. WarpMove completion also calls NotifyHomingWarpEnd with bSkipViewInterp = (180 == this value).

WarpAdjustTargetSimulateType.simple: Chooses how the game predicts a recently hit target's movement when picking a teleport landing spot, including knockback and sideways drift.
WarpAdjustTargetSimulateType.technical: uint8-backed EGameWarpAdjustTargetSimulateType (None, DeviationOnlySimulate, BlowSimulate, Invalid=255). Simulation requires type != None, a valid target, a clear damage-action slot, no collision locks and the owner as last attacker. DeviationOnlySimulate sweeps the target's predicted vertical motion then keeps WarpDirection; BlowSimulate approaches against the target's last blow/move direction with wall sliding or push-out. BlowSimulate dominates the exports.

bFollowGroundEnabled.simple: Chooses whether the character stays close to the ground while following the target. This also changes how arrival and falling are handled.
bFollowGroundEnabled.technical: Bool. It is inverted into bHomingIgnoresGroundFollowing at start, gates RangeZ usage and AngleZ bending, enables the follow-ground blocked arrival test, is passed to SetInertia, and drives fall-curve handling.

FollowGroundCheckDistance.simple: How far ahead the game checks for ground while the character follows the target. A blocked path counts as arriving.
FollowGroundCheckDistance.technical: World units added to owner capsule radius for the forward ground test; when blocked, homing counts as arrived.

FollowGroundFallGravity.simple: How quickly the character falls while following the ground during this move. Higher values pull the character down faster.
FollowGroundFallGravity.technical: Float. BuildFallCurve uses it with Global.JumpFall_Speed_Max, then MoveState.FallGravity is set to this value and vertical position is advanced by the sampled fall speed.

FollowGroundIgnoreStepDistance.simple: Helps decide whether a small step or low obstacle blocks ground following. The exact threshold behavior is unclear.
FollowGroundIgnoreStepDistance.technical: World units passed as the step-distance parameter of Movement_IsFollowGroundBlocked (with 1000.0 as the other threshold).

bSuperArmorEnabled.simple: Chooses whether the character can power through hits while this attack is tracking. The attack's own armor setting takes over when the attack activates.
bSuperArmorEnabled.technical: Bool copied into FGameCharacterAction_AttackBase.bSuperArmorEnabled and exposed through IsSuperArmorEnabled while the homing phase is active; cleared on the homing-failure animation. ActivateAttack replaces it with AttackRow.bSuperArmorEnabled on all normal activation paths, including non-warp homing.

bHyperArmorEnabled.simple: Chooses whether the character keeps attacking through hits while tracking. The attack's own armor setting takes over when the attack activates.
bHyperArmorEnabled.technical: Bool copied into the attack action alongside super armor, exposed via IsHyperArmorEnabled; cleared on homing failure. ActivateAttack replaces it with AttackRow.bHyperArmorEnabled on all normal activation paths.

bExternalForceEnabled.simple: Chooses whether this move pushes the target outward for a short time. The push fires when the path between them is clear.
bExternalForceEnabled.technical: Bool. When true, StartHoming arms ExternalForceInterp and TickHoming traces to the secondary target; on a clear trace it issues a push-out request.

ExternalForceRange.simple: How wide the outward push is when this move sends the target away. Larger values reach farther.
ExternalForceRange.technical: World units passed as the final argument of BattleManager.AddPushOutRequest when external force fires.

ExternalForceStrength_Start.simple: How strong the outward push is when it begins. Higher values push harder at the start.
ExternalForceStrength_Start.technical: Value used to start ExternalForceInterp; TickHoming reads GetCurrent() as push strength.

ExternalForceStrength_End.simple: How strong the outward push is by the time it ends. Higher values keep the push stronger near the end.

ExternalForceStrength_InterpolateTime.simple: How long the outward push takes to change from its starting strength to its ending strength.

ExternalForceStrength_EasingType.simple: Chooses how the push strength changes over its short duration, with the usual setting easing out gently near the end.
ExternalForceStrength_EasingType.technical: EGameEasingType converted by ShikigamiMovement_ToEasingFunc in ExternalForceInterp.Start.

ExternalForceStrength_Blend_Exp.simple: Shapes how the push strength changes during the move. The exact feel of this setting is unclear.
ExternalForceStrength_Blend_Exp.technical: Float passed as the blend exponent in ExternalForceInterp.Start.

ExternalForceGravityCorrect.simple: Adjusts how gravity is accounted for when the outward push happens. Most moves use the standard setting, with a few lower ones.
ExternalForceGravityCorrect.technical: Float passed to BattleManager.AddPushOutRequest alongside the push point, strength and range. Exported as 1.0 in 266 rows and 0.2 in 2 (the C++ constructor default is 0.0).

notes: Five exported shards (ActionHomingDataTable1..5; 59/59/59/65/26 rows = 268 unique keys, no repeated keys) share the 48-field FGameDataTableRow_ActionHoming schema. The manager loads all five into ActionHomingDataTables in that order; Action_FindActionHomingRow returns the first table holding the id (bCheckNone depends on the caller).

No localization variants of this group were exported. Read-only exports are partial, so complete retail row coverage is not claimed; within the export, all 229 distinct non-None AttackRow Id_ActionHoming / Id_CancelAttackActionHoming values resolve to a homing row, while 39 homing rows are reached only through ID remaps, hardcoded lookups or other special paths.

Native types: 4 FName fields (Id and three animation names), 5 uint8-backed enums, 5 bool flags and 34 float numeric fields; there are no array-index fields. Distances are world units, times/durations seconds, Rotation_Yaw/AngleZ/pitch/yaw degrees, and speeds units/second.

The C++ constructor initializes every reflected member to zero/false/None; exported rows override them, notably Rotation_Speed_Blend_Exp 2.0 (267 rows; one 1.0), Speed_Blend_Exp 1.0 (261 rows; seven 2.0) and ExternalForceGravityCorrect 1.0 (266 rows; two 0.2). EGameEasingType::None maps through ShikigamiMovement_ToEasingFunc to EEasingFunc::EaseOut, so "None" is not no easing.

Rotation_Time = -1.0 is a real exported sentinel (9 rows) that suppresses RotateTowardLocation/StartRotationEase; Rotation_Angle_Limit and Rotation_Yaw are 0.0 in all exported rows, CharacterAnimation_Failure is None in all 268, and no row uses EightWay or any enum Invalid=255.

Character homing's timers/interpolators arm only when Homing_Time_Max > 0 and a secondary target is valid; without that, TickHoming is a no-op and attack homing falls through to ActivateAttack, although StartHoming can still issue EightWay/default rotation calls outside the target gate.

Attack-row Warp (not WarpMove) takes CharacterAnimation/WeaponAnimation from AttackRow; homing-row armor flags set during Phase 1 are replaced by AttackRow values in ActivateAttack except when a timeout failure animation early-outs. Shikigami attacks use the homing row's CharacterAnimation unconditionally, and their homing tick uses only range/delay/time/speed/rotation/AngleZ fields (no warp, ground-follow, armor, external-force or HomingResult behavior).
The source is reconstructed C++; retail RVA comments are provenance, not byte-match claims, and Blueprint/retail-only behavior not present in these headers or exports is not asserted.

usages.detail: Loads ActionHomingDataTable1..5 into the ordered ActionHomingDataTables array.
Shared first-matching-table finder over the five homing shards; honors bCheckNone for None ids.
Resolves the homing row from AttackRow.Id_ActionHoming or Id_CancelAttackActionHoming and stores it on the attack action.
Virtual ResolveActionHomingId hook applied to both AttackRow homing ids before lookup.
With the CursedEnergyAttack2 buff, remaps A..I/AUTO ids to _2 variants and resolves unlisted ids to None.
Against a finish target, remaps attacks C/D to their _2 homing ids (other ids become None).
While the weapon-drawn/variation flag is set, remaps first-hit A/B/C ids to _02 variants.
Suppresses CN_240_ATTACKB_01 homing (returns None) when the target is within that row's WarpTargetDistance.
Third normal-attack start looks up hardcoded CP_050_ATTACKD_02 and calls StartHoming directly.
Character-specific repeat gate uses HomingDistance.
Hardcoded cursed-energy warp-start gate uses WarpDistance; FName matching is case-insensitive against exported CP_051_ATTACKG_* rows.
Shikigami attack caches the resolved row and starts shikigami homing; plays its CharacterAnimation on success.
Shikigami StartHoming uses Homing_Time_Max/Min, HomingDistance, speed/rotation eases and Rotation_Yaw/Angle_Limit only.
Shikigami tick reads range/delay/time/speed/AngleZ from the cached row and uses EaseOut inertia.
Character StartHoming validates Homing_Time_Max, arms interpolators and selects behavior by ActionHomingType.
Character TickHoming applies range/time gates, ground following, warp and external force.
TickHomingMove applies AngleZ and vertical direction correction.
StartRotationEase/RotateTowardLocation ignore negative time, implementing the exported -1 Rotation_Time sentinel.
Computes warp destination using warp distance, target distance, pitch/yaw adjust and simulate type.
Applies homing animations and armor flags when homing starts; only Warp uses AttackRow animations here.
Plays the failure animation and clears armor when homing timed out.
Hit-quota early exit reapplies Inertia_Rate/Time and bFollowGroundEnabled from the cached row.
NotifyHomingStart forwards the row to ActionController::OnHomingWarpStart for warp types.
OnHomingWarpStart reads the row Id to special-case CP_270_ATTACKH_01.
